grouped_facts.fact: Cross-project refs ({{ ref() }}) work across dbt projects on Enterprise and Enterprise+ plans, enabling references to models in other projects to support multi-project deployments.
grouped_facts.quote: "Cross-project references ... is the foundational feature that enables the multi-project deployments. `{{ ref() }}`s now work across dbt projects"

grouped_facts.fact: dbt Catalog provides full, cross-project lineage to discover dependencies across multiple projects.
grouped_facts.quote: "Catalog ... complete with full, cross-project lineage."

grouped_facts.fact: Cross-project references require each project name to be unique in your dbt account.
grouped_facts.quote: Cross-project references require that each project `name` be unique in your dbt account.

grouped_facts.fact: A dbt Enterprise-tier plan is required to set up multiple projects and reference models across them.
grouped_facts.quote: Yes, a dbt Enterprise-tier plan is required to set up multiple projects and reference models across them.

grouped_facts.fact: Groups let you organize DAG nodes by logical area and assign an owner to the entire group for governance.
grouped_facts.quote: "With groups, you can organize nodes in your dbt DAG that share a logical connection ... and assign an owner to the entire group."

grouped_facts.fact: Access configs allow you to control who can reference models, enforcing cross-project reference permissions.
grouped_facts.quote: "Access configs allow you to control who can reference models."

grouped_facts.fact: Model Versions provide versioning so teams can treat models as stable APIs for cross-project adoption and deprecation.
grouped_facts.quote: "Model versioning is the mechanism to allow graceful adoption and deprecation of models as they evolve."

grouped_facts.fact: To deprecate a model (or downgrade its access), mark it with deprecation_date to deliver a warning to all downstream consumers.
grouped_facts.quote: they should mark that model for deprecation (using deprecation_date), which will deliver a warning to all downstream consumers of that model.

grouped_facts.fact: Model Contracts let you set explicit expectations on data shape to prevent upstream changes breaking downstream consumers.
grouped_facts.quote: "Model Contracts  data contracts set explicit expectations on the shape of the data to ensure data changes upstream ... don't break downstream consumers' data products."

grouped_facts.fact: Contracts can only be applied at the model level and apply to the entire model, including all output columns; you cannot apply contracts to sources or to part of a model.
grouped_facts.quote: No, contracts can only be applied at the model level. No. A contract applies to an entire model, including all columns in the model’s output.

grouped_facts.fact: Cross-project refs resolve to Production by default; if a project defines both Production and Staging, refs from development and Staging environments resolve to Staging while refs from Production resolve to Production.
grouped_facts.quote: By default, cross-project references resolve to the "Production" deployment environment... If a project defines both a "Production" environment and a "Staging" environment, then cross-project references from development and "Staging" environments will resolve to "Staging," whereas only references coming from "Production" environments will resolve to "Production."

grouped_facts.fact: Protected is the default access: protected models can be referenced by any model within the same dbt project or when the project is installed as a package.
grouped_facts.quote: Protected: Models with a protected access modifier can be referenced by any other model within the same dbt project or when the project is installed as a package. This is the default setting for all models...

grouped_facts.fact: Private models are referenceable only by models within the same group.
grouped_facts.quote: Private: A model with a private access modifier is only referenceable by models within the same group.

grouped_facts.fact: Running `dbt build --select +model` will not run upstream models in other projects unless those upstream projects are installed as packages (source code).
grouped_facts.quote: No, unless upstream projects are installed as packages (source code). In that case, the models in project installed as a project become "your" models, and you can select or run them.

grouped_facts.fact: To enable bidirectional project dependencies, each project must run and produce public models before the other can take a dependency on it.
grouped_facts.quote: Each project must run and produce public models before the original producer project can take a dependency on the original consumer project.

grouped_facts.fact: Built-in job commands are chained; if one run step fails the entire job fails with an "Error" status.
grouped_facts.quote: During a job run, built-in commands are "chained" together and if one run step fails, the entire job fails with an "Error" status.

grouped_facts.fact: Checkbox steps like 'Generate docs on run' or 'Run source freshness' can fail without failing the whole job if subsequent steps pass.
grouped_facts.quote: If the step fails, the job can succeed if subsequent steps pass.

grouped_facts.fact: By default a deploy job's Commands section includes the dbt build command.
grouped_facts.quote: By default, it includes the `dbt build` command.

grouped_facts.fact: By default a job inherits the dbt version from its environment; changing the job-level version is discouraged except for upgrades.
grouped_facts.quote: By default, its set to inherit the dbt version from the environment. dbt Labs strongly recommends that you don't change the default setting.

grouped_facts.fact: Intervals scheduling runs every N hours from midnight UTC; subsequent runs keep the same offset (e.g., 00:04 -> 02:04 for Every 2 hours).
grouped_facts.quote: If you choose **Every 2 hours**, the job will run every 2 hours from midnight UTC. ... if the previous scheduled pipeline ran at 00:04 UTC, the next run will be at 02:04 UTC.

grouped_facts.fact: dbt job schedules use UTC and do not translate to local time or account for daylight savings.
grouped_facts.quote: dbt uses Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and does not account for translations to your specific timezone or take into consideration daylight savings time.

grouped_facts.fact: Developer plans enforce a minimum cron scheduling interval of 10 minutes; Starter/Enterprise plans have no execution-frequency restrictions.
grouped_facts.quote: Developer plans: dbt sets a minimum interval of every 10 minutes for scheduling jobs. ... Starter, Enterprise, and Enterprise+ plans: No restrictions on job execution frequency.

grouped_facts.fact: The 'Run when another job finishes' trigger (job chaining) requires a Starter or Enterprise-tier dbt plan.
grouped_facts.quote: For the [Trigger on job completion] feature, your dbt account must be on the [Starter or an Enterprise-tier] plan.

grouped_facts.fact: Job 'Threads' defaults to 4; increasing threads raises model execution concurrency.
grouped_facts.quote: By default, its set to 4 threads. Increase the thread count to increase model execution concurrency.

grouped_facts.fact: Compare changes 'No deferral' is default; options are 'Environment' or 'This Job' and deferral-to-environment compares against the environment's manifest.json.
grouped_facts.quote: By default, its set to **No deferral**. Select either **Environment** or **This Job**... deferral to an environment is more efficient as dbt will compare against the project representation (which is stored in the `manifest.json`) of the last successful deploy job run that executed in the deferred environment.
